also: on which syllable is the stress?

terms.comment: Quintilian’s word, made as a translation of Greek προσῳδία (ad + cantus): the accent that falls on one syllable of a word. In late Latin it is also a blast of trumpets (Amm.). The beat of a verse is ictus, which is not the same thing as the word’s accent. To put the stress on a syllable is accentum in syllabā pōnere (Traupman 245).

sources: Lewis & Short: accentus · Lewis & Short: ictus

phrases.latin: ēvenit, ut metrī quoque condiciō mūtet accentum
phrases.english: it happens that the needs of the metre also change the accent

phrases.latin: In quā syllabā accentum pōnimus? — Aut in antepaenultimā aut in paenultimā.
phrases.english: On which syllable do we place the stress? — On the antepenult or the penult.
